first.rationale: Verify the two most directly relevant records: onboarding completion and activation messaging. The simultaneous declines point to simplifying onboarding as the best sustainable response, while avoiding promotional pricing because its prior acquisition lift came with materially worse 30-day retention. A standard experiment can test completion, time-to-value, activation, and qualified revenue quality.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. It directly addresses the 4% completion decline and has the strongest verified downstream evidence: completion improved 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention increased 3%. Track qualified revenue, activation, time-to-value, completion, and retention to ensure the lift is sustainable. Activation messaging is a credible fallback, but onboarding offers broader leverage across both current problems.

final2.rationale: Run a tightly targeted, time-limited pricing defense for demonstrably price-sensitive SMB accounts, with strict retention, gross-margin, and qualified-revenue guardrails. The deeper competitor cut and doubled churn risk justify a tactical response, but prior evidence shows promotional pricing materially harmed 30-day retention, so this should not become a broad rollout or replace the sustainable onboarding work.
